items.text: The teenage daughter of Morteza Haddad Shalkouhi lit a candle at her father's grave as part of the 'One Candle, One Name, One Memory' campaign. Morteza Haddad Shalkouhi was killed on January 9, 2026, in Rasht. This video was released by Iran International.

A citizen secretly recorded a video from the flogging execution room. This video will soon be published as a detailed testimony. The purpose is to expose the injustice and humiliating punishments faced by Iranian people.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a ship was targeted in the Strait of Hormuz. The governor of Qeshm stated that one person was killed and three others injured in the incident. He identified the United States as the perpetrator of the attack.

The Tehran prosecutor has filed charges against the host, producer, and two guests of the online program "Ba Zia" for making false economic claims and unsubstantiated statements. This action was taken due to the accusations made in the program. More details have been published by Harana News Agency.

Romina Pourmokhtari was appointed as Sweden's Minister of Climate and Environment. She became the youngest minister in Sweden's history after this appointment. A special interview with her is available on Iran International's YouTube channel.

Faisal bin Farhan, Saudi Arabia's foreign minister, stated that GCC countries do not accept attacks on their territory or vital interests. He emphasized the importance of national security and freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. He added that stability in these routes is crucial for energy security and global trade.

Majid Ibn al-Reza, acting defense minister, stated that the Islamic Republic would perform much more powerfully technologically in case of another war. He said the displayed defense capability is only a small part of the actual capacity. He also emphasized that the Islamic Republic relies on internal capabilities to ensure its security.

Six years ago on this day, Navid Afkari, an Iranian wrestler and protester of the August 2018 protests, was executed. The execution took place despite requests and reactions from international and human rights organizations. Navid Afkari was executed by the Iranian government on September 12, 2020.

Shahbaz Sharif, the Prime Minister of Pakistan, condemned the proxy attacks by the Islamic Republic on southern Saudi Arabia. Yahya Saree, the military spokesperson for the Houthis, confirmed the attacks using ballistic missiles and drones. The attacks targeted ammunition depots and command centers of a military base in southern Saudi Arabia.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated after the BRICS summit in New Delhi that he hopes the malicious intentions of the US in the region will be thwarted. He emphasized that BRICS countries favor a multipolar world and increased economic cooperation. Opposition to unilateral sanctions and expansion of trade with national currencies were also discussed.

Donald Trump stated that the Iran issue might end before the US midterm elections but will definitely end after them. He said Iran really wants to reach an agreement, but the deal must be right. Trump also commented that the Gulf countries' meetings with Iran are their own business.
An abandoned newborn was found in one of the streets of Nurabad in Lorestan province. This incident took place in the city of Nurabad. More details are published by Harana News Agency.
A car sank into the ground on North Ferdowsi Street in Nishapur due to land subsidence. This incident occurred because of the ground sinking. No reports of casualties have been announced.

A car sank into the ground on North Ferdowsi Street in Nishapur due to ground subsidence. This incident occurred because of changes in the land. No further details about the car or driver have been reported.

Abbas Basafa announced that newly registered cars valued over one billion tomans receive 110 liters of gasoline monthly at 10,000 tomans per liter and do not get gasoline quotas at 1,500 and 3,000 tomans rates. Newly registered cars under one billion tomans receive the normal gasoline quota. Personal passenger cars with normal quotas receive 60 liters of gasoline at 1,500 tomans and 50 liters at 3,000 tomans monthly.

Ali Sarai's brother joined the 'One Candle, One Name, One Memory' campaign and lit a candle for him. Ali Sarai was shot and killed by officers on January 9, 2026, in Azadshahr, Mashhad. His brother said his path continues.

A group of Iranians gathered in central Brussels on Sunday, September 13. The gathering was held to commemorate Mahsa Zhina Amini and those who died in the protests in Iran. It also aimed to support political prisoners and protest executions in Iran.

The German government announced a significant decrease in asylum applications. The rate of support granted to Iranian applicants after case reviews has risen to over 42 percent. This report was published by Ali Hassanpour from Iran International.
A man in Tehran was tried in criminal court for the murder of his wife and two young children. This incident took place in Tehran province. The trial of this individual is ongoing.

The coalition of political forces in Iranian Kurdistan has called on people to hold a general strike on Wednesday, September 25. This strike coincides with the fourth anniversary of the killing of Mahsa Zhina Amini and the start of the "Woman, Life, Freedom" movement. The coalition described the strike as a civil response to security and economic crises.

Heavy vehicle drivers are trapped at the Chazabeh border after it was closed. They have been stuck there for three days without water, food, or facilities. This was reported in a video sent to Iran International.

The war involving Iran and restrictions on tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz have increased the return of the American investment fund "Breakwave Tanker Shipping" by 3600 percent. The oil shipping rates in Middle Eastern routes have risen by nearly 500 percent compared to last year. This situation is due to difficulties passing through the Strait of Hormuz and increased maritime transport costs.

Ahmad Reza Radan, the chief of police, stated that Alireza Beiranvand must choose between Malavan or Fajr Sepasi teams for his military service. He emphasized that military service is mandatory for everyone with no exceptions. The champion soldier law does not apply to Beiranvand, and he must complete his service.

Hossein Rasouli Nasab, a detainee from the December 2025 protests in Shandiz, was sentenced to death by the Mashhad Revolutionary Court. His charges include waging war against God, destruction of public property, burning religious centers, and conspiracy against national security. He is currently imprisoned in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

Javad Hosseini, head of the Welfare Organization, said there are currently 10,350,000 elderly people in the country, making up nearly 14 percent of the population. He predicted the share of Iran's population over 60 will reach 31 percent by the year 1430. Hosseini warned that necessary facilities and programs are not in place to match the speed of aging.

The Civil Registration Organization announced that artificial intelligence and blockchain technologies have been used in the new national ID cards. This measure aims to enhance security and improve services. No further details were provided.

A citizen lit a candle in Behesht Sakineh, Karaj, in memory of protesters killed in December 2025. This was done as part of the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." He conveyed that they are remembered.

More than three thousand teenagers from Markazi province were sent to Rahian-e Noor camps in the operational areas of western Iran. This action is against Iran's commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child. Iran had pledged not to involve children in military activities.

There is widespread disruption at Iran's borders with Iraq and Turkey, affecting land trade and export routes. Truck waiting times at the borders have increased. Concerns have also been raised about reduced trade between the two countries due to US sanctions.

Mohsen Hashemi stated that officials of the Islamic Republic used metro stations as offices during the 12-day and 40-day wars. No safe places or public shelters were introduced for citizens during these wars. Additionally, a citizen's house in Vahdat Town, Karaj, was targeted in an attack in Esfand and remains destroyed.

Eight female prisoners in Iran face death sentences on political, security, and protest-related charges. Some of these death sentences have been confirmed, while others are still in preliminary stages. These sentences were issued by revolutionary courts in various cities.

Jared Kushner stated that the US government used Israel's global isolation after its attack on Hamas leaders in Doha for mediation. He described the attack as unsuccessful and causing Israel's isolation. The US used this situation to pressure and reach a ceasefire agreement.

According to Harana, at least eight female prisoners in Iran have been sentenced to death in political, security, and protest-related cases. The death sentences of two of them have been confirmed by the Supreme Court. The charges include rebellion, waging war against God, and corruption on earth.

The mother of Arya Alidoost lit a candle in the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" to honor her son. Arya Alidoost was killed on January 8, 2026, in Lahijan. His mother said that her son and his companions gave their lives for the freedom of Iran.

A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that the price of desmopressin has increased about fivefold in recent months. This medication is used to control excessive urination and thirst caused by antidiuretic hormone deficiency. The price increase has raised concerns.
Sheikh Zahed Shahabi, a citizen of Saqez, remains detained in Saqez prison after about six months. His situation in prison remains uncertain. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Mehdi Hashemi, a 125 kg wrestler, was severely injured in a collision with a Nissan pickup in Juybar, Mazandaran. He is currently hospitalized in intensive care in Sari and is in a coma. Hashemi suffered broken ribs, internal bleeding, and serious injuries to his skull, ribs, and lungs.

Barcelona defeated Levante 4-2 in the fifth week of La Liga with a double from Lamine Yamal and goals from Xavi Simons and Ademi. Yamal scored doubles for the third consecutive game, a feat last achieved by Messi. Barcelona recorded their fifth consecutive victory and remains unbeaten.

The New York Times reported that Hossein Taeb was the planner of the attack on ships during the Tehran-Washington ceasefire. After the attack, a verbal dispute occurred between Masoud Pezeshkian and Ahmad Vahidi. Ahmad Vahidi and the Supreme National Security Council claimed to be unaware of the attack.
A woman was arrested in Masal County for causing public disturbance on social media. She was referred to the judicial authorities. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Donald Trump stated that Iranian officials are continuously contacting for a deal with the US. He emphasized that the deal must be right and the Iran issue may end before the US midterm elections. Additionally, the IRGC warned American ships after attacks on two commercial vessels near Qeshm.

Hossein Samsami announced the uncertain fate of more than 56 million barrels of oil. Over 86 million barrels were allocated on credit to one person. Only 30 million barrels have been transferred to the final buyer.

Mohammadreza Mastan Saljouqi, a 66-year-old citizen and a war-related nerve and psychological injury victim, has been detained in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad for over 9 months without a clear status. His case's interrogation process started in Esfand 1404 at the Mashhad prosecutor's office, but no trial has been held yet. He has attended several interrogation sessions but remains in detention.

Representatives of Israel and Lebanon will meet in Rome in October to discuss a security agreement mediated by the US. The agreement aims to reduce conflicts along the border between the two countries. Additionally, the ambassadors of both countries will meet in Washington next week.

The Supreme Court confirmed the death sentence of a woman accused of murder. Additionally, five prisoners in various provinces were released from the death penalty with the consent of the victims' families. These prisoners were in Isfahan, Lorestan, Qazvin, Bandar Abbas, and Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari.

Bahman Modirzadeh, a member of the Qotur City Council in West Azerbaijan province, has been held in Khoy prison for 41 days. His situation remains uncertain. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Javad Nekounam, head coach of Tractor, said that Alireza Beiranvand's absence in the match against Shabab Al Ahli is important for the team and defense line. Nekounam mentioned Parsa Jafari as Beiranvand's replacement and expressed full confidence in his readiness. He also emphasized the importance of starting the competition well and having the best performance.

Mehdi Mahdavi Azad stated that Mohsen Rezaei's appointment as Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council was made with direct intervention by Mojtaba Khamenei. He highlighted Rezaei's 47-year background in military and foreign policy. Rezaei's role in behind-the-scenes relations and economic networks of the Islamic Republic was also noted.
The audio version of Titraval with Niusha Saremi has been released. It discusses conflicts at the top of the government. It also questions whether Taeb ordered attacks on ships.

Mohammad Kaabi, a citizen from Shush county, was arrested by the Intelligence Organization forces of the IRGC. The arrest took place on the afternoon of Saturday, September 12. His place of detention is unknown.

Masoud Pezeshkian described the IRGC's attack on three commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz as reckless and irresponsible. He contacted the IRGC commander demanding accountability. The commander denied responsibility and stated the operation was unauthorized and unknown to the Supreme National Security Council.

Brad Cooper, the commander of CENTCOM, said there is no concern about the shortage of US interceptor missiles. He stated that US forces are prepared to face any situation. These remarks were made amid ongoing clashes with the Islamic Republic.

Several workers on the border wall construction project in Golshan county reported wage arrears. These workers have requested attention to their payment situation. This issue was reported by Harana News Agency.

Ali Daei spoke about the existence of mafia in Iran's automobile industry. He stated that mafia exists in all parts of society, including football and automobiles. This interview took place on the sidelines of the Tehran Auto Show.

Disciplinary cases have been filed against 40 students of the University of Tehran for burning the flag. This is related to the student protests in March of last year. The charge is described as "insult and burning of the flag."

Yesterday, several job seekers from the Nissan area of Howeyzeh county held a protest near the North Azadegan oil field. The protesters demanded justice in hiring and priority for local forces. This protest took place in Howeyzeh county.

Israel's Defense Minister Yisrael Katz stated that the Israeli army will maintain control over the Al-Taher mountain range in southern Lebanon and will destroy anyone approaching it. After destroying Hezbollah's tunnels, the Israeli army withdrew from the mountain range and positioned its forces along the 'yellow line'. Attacks continue to prevent Hezbollah's return, and coordination with the Lebanese government is underway to deploy Lebanese army forces in evacuated areas.

On September 12, several protests were held by Social Security retirees in various cities. Steel industry retirees in Isfahan and housing movement applicants in Shiraz also held protests. Motorcycle couriers in Lahijan went on strike in protest of current conditions.

The French army announced that the Aspides mission to protect ships in the Bab al-Mandab Strait continues. The Houthi military spokesperson stated that navigation is safe for all ships except Saudi vessels. These statements were made amid regional tensions.

Omid Memarian stated that despite the growing Muslim population in the US, memories of the 9/11 attacks and wars with extremist groups have increased negative views of Islam. He added that generalizing extremist actions to all Muslims has played a significant role in this perception. This issue has intensified over the past 25 years.

Mohsen Modir Shanechi said the US primarily uses economic and financial tools to besiege the Islamic Republic and employs military power if necessary. He identified inflation as a key indicator of the Islamic Republic's resilience. Rising dollar and essential goods prices indicate increasing pressure on Iran's economy.

The Saudi Foreign Ministry announced that the east-west oil pipeline was attacked by drones launched from Iraq. Saudi Arabia has decided not to take retaliatory action at this stage. The country reserves the right to take all necessary measures to protect its security.

Trump stated that the US is at war with the biggest supporter of terrorism. These remarks were made in the audio version of the program 24 with Fardad Farahzad. The topic is related to war and terrorism.

Georgi Gvelesiani, former player of Persepolis and the Georgian national team, announced the end of his professional career. He spoke about playing with chronic knee injuries and fighting until the last moment. Gvelesiani thanked his fans and companions and left the football field with pride.

The US Central Command announced that American forces have redirected 99 commercial ships by September 10 to ensure the enforcement of the naval blockade against Iran. The USS Boxer and the Boxer amphibious group are involved in this operation. An image of a US Navy MH-60R Seahawk helicopter has been released.
In the audio version of Harf Akhar with Pouria Zeraati, the issue of several Islamic Republic officials contacting Mossad to eliminate Mojtaba was discussed.

Esmail Baghai, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated that the Strait of Hormuz is under full control of the Islamic Republic's armed forces. He mentioned that after the Islamabad agreement, the security situation improved but the US violated the agreement. Additionally, negotiations between the Islamic Republic and Oman regarding the Strait of Hormuz are ongoing.

A birthday ceremony for Fathollah Avari was held at his gravesite. Fathollah Avari was one of the detainees from December 2025 who was executed on June 3, 2026. This news is based on a video received by Iran International.

Hadi Choopan, former Mr. Olympia champion, said in a video interview that he tried for 10 years to help Hani Rambod grow. He added that he never thought the day would come when Hani Rambod would be the reason for his downfall.

A citizen posted a video showing a queue of heavy vehicles at the Chabahar cargo terminal. He says the 250-liter gasoline quota is sold for eight million tomans. Also, they have to wait in line for hours to get the quota.
The mother of Matin Montazer-ozur distributed food in memory of her killed son. Matin Montazer-ozur was 32 years old and from Gorgan. He was shot dead on January 7, 2026, in the city of Shahroud.

An Anthropic researcher resigned due to fears about the future of artificial intelligence. He warns that a self-improving superintelligence could become a threat to human survival within this decade. He also raised questions about who should decide how and where this technology is used if even its creators are uncertain about controlling it.

Reza Najafi, Iran's representative to the IAEA, said the US might use the new IAEA resolution to escalate conflicts and start military operations against Iran. He called the IAEA's decision to refer Iran's case to the UN Security Council political and stated that Iran's cooperation with the agency continues. Najafi emphasized that Iran will decide its response after assessing the resolution's consequences.

Jamshid Barzegar said the September 11 attacks changed US foreign policy and global developments. Fighting terrorist groups and the Islamic Republic has become a priority for Washington. Linking the anniversary of September 11 to the current war against the Islamic Republic indicates the continuation of the counter-terrorism strategy.
Videos sent to Iran International show a large fire in the Ashkan mountains in the south of Noorabad, Mamasani on Friday, September 11.

A video shows that on Friday, 20 Shahrivar, at a gathering of Iranians living in Hanover, Germany, some supporters of Palestine were also present. Police formed a line between the two groups. This event took place at the gathering site.

The US State Department's "Rewards for Justice" program announced it has set rewards of up to $10 million for information on a number of senior al-Qaeda leaders based in Iran. The program said these individuals use Iran as a safe haven for planning and executing attacks against the US and its allies. In the published poster, rewards ranging from $3 million to $10 million have been set for information on some of these individuals, and people have been asked to provide their information.

According to TankerTrackers, the total crude oil exports of Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, UAE, and Oman from the US blockade line exceeded 10 million barrels per day for the first time in two months. This increase occurred after the practical halt of the Islamabad agreement. Iran's crude oil exports remain at zero.

Pouria Bakhtiari stated that during Ebrahim Raisi's government, he was asked to teach economic topics to Raisi. These teachings were prepared as short texts for animation and cartoon production. The content was designed to be under three minutes because Raisi's mind is fleeting.

A video has been released showing Shoja Khalilzadeh insulting several players of the Tractor team. The Football Federation's disciplinary committee last week suspended Khodadad Azizi for four months due to insults. Khalilzadeh has a history of offensive behavior towards rival teams' fans.

Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of India, met and talked with Masoud Pezeshkian, the head of the Islamic Republic government, on Friday, 20 Shahrivar, in Delhi. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the annual BRICS member countries summit. The topics discussed in the meeting were not disclosed.
A video shows heavy vehicles in Karaj standing in a long queue to receive diesel fuel. The video was received by Iran International. The queue situation in Karaj is depicted.

Reza Pahlavi stated on the anniversary of 9/11 that Iranians and Americans have never been enemies and that freedom is a shared value. He identified Islamic extremism as a common enemy that has held his country hostage. He also emphasized that freedom is the foundation of America and the goal Iranians are fighting for today.

Saleheh Akbari, a nurse and rescue instructor, was shot and killed on the evening of January 12 in Ardabil. This happened during a security forces raid to arrest her husband. Farbod Sarvandi's report covers the life of this couple and their fate during the protests.

The Houthis have gained control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea coasts, and three strategic Yemeni islands after a week of advances. Yemeni government sources stated that the group has full control over the Bab al-Mandeb area and the islands of Mayun, Greater Hanis, and Lesser Hanis. The Houthi military spokesperson announced that passage through Bab al-Mandeb is safe for all ships except Saudi vessels.

The CENTCOM commander traveled to Saudi Arabia to hold meetings regarding the recent Houthi advances in Yemen. The Houthis have taken control of the port city of Al-Mokha and the southwestern coastal strip of Yemen. Al Jazeera has not released further details about these meetings.

Masoud Pezeshkian, the head of the Islamic Republic government, attended a pre-BRICS summit in New Delhi on Friday, September 20. The meeting was held before the main BRICS summit. Vladimir Putin, Cyril Ramaphosa, and Narendra Modi were also present at the session.

Hassan Ameli, the Friday prayer leader of Ardabil, stated that before the US attack, Bab al-Mandeb and the Strait of Hormuz were open and served the global economy. He said Trump's attack closed both routes, and now Iran will determine the oil price. Ameli described this as a power greater than the atomic bomb.

The judiciary announced the seizure of 240 properties belonging to Iranian citizens living abroad due to alleged connections with hostile countries and actions against national security. Bank accounts of 182 individuals have been blocked. Over two thousand inquiries were made to the Central Bank regarding citizens' accounts.

Iran International conducted an Instagram survey about the impact of the January killings and ongoing war on people's mental health. About 38,000 people participated, and 94% said their anger is triggered more quickly than in previous years. Farshad Motaghi discussed this topic in the program "Pivast."

Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of War, stated at the 25th anniversary commemoration of the 9/11 attacks that the US has destroyed "the world's biggest state sponsor of terrorism" in the past six months. He added that the Iranian government has supported terrorist attacks against Americans for decades, killing thousands. Hegseth emphasized that the US ensures the Islamic Republic does not acquire nuclear weapons and that economic pressure on Iran is increasing daily.

A Houthi fighter announced the capture of the port of Al-Mokha on the Red Sea coast in western Yemen. He stated that Saleh's forces have fled and the Houthis are advancing towards the Bab al-Mandab area. These images were released on Thursday and Friday, coinciding with the Houthis' advance along Yemen's western coast.

Hussein Kaidi, an 18-year-old young man from Andimeshk, was shot dead by government agents in front of his home on the evening of January 9, 2026. His mother stated in a video that her son posed no threat and that she will pursue the truth about his death. She emphasized that she has not buried her grief and is seeking justice.
On Thursday night in Golestan province, rainfall caused flooding in some streets and alleys in the cities of Galikesh and Gonbad Kavus. This was shown in videos received by Iran International.

The official 25th anniversary ceremony of the September 11 terrorist attacks is being held at the Pentagon with the presence of Donald Trump and victims' families. The names of 184 victims of the Pentagon attack are read during the ceremony. An Iran International reporter is covering the event from New York.

Representatives from several Middle Eastern countries at the MEID conference in Washington viewed the end of the Islamic Republic as beneficial for the region but not certain. The Islamic Republic is severely weakened, but its collapse is not imminent and may take one to three years. Iran's economic situation was assessed as dire, and about 80% of Iranians oppose the government.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International criticizing the poor asphalt condition in Rasht Industrial City. He pointed out problems caused by the damaged street surfaces. The video was sent to Iran International.

The Swedish Ministry of Justice stated that the Islamic Republic has conducted activities over several years that threaten the country's security. The ministry said the Islamic Republic has used criminal networks for violent actions. This information was provided in response to Iran International.

The Jerusalem Post reported that after a meeting between Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump at the White House, a strategic plan was approved to create conditions for regime change in Iran. This news was published by Iran International. An interview with Ashkan Safaei was conducted on this matter.

The carcass of a large Bryde's whale was found on Sunday, 22 Shahrivar, on the coast of Bandar Charak. This species usually exceeds 10 meters in length and weighs several tons. The cause of death is still unknown, but in previous cases, collisions with ship propellers have been the most common cause.

Israeli army radio announced that after completing the operation to destroy Hezbollah tunnels, Israeli forces have left the Ali al-Taher heights. The forces have moved to rear positions. Israel still maintains fire control over the area.

Bloomberg reported that Iran's crude oil and condensate loading decreased by about 74% in August, reaching 247,000 barrels per day. Iran's oil exports remain severely limited due to the US naval blockade. Iran's crude oil reserves have reached the highest level in several months.
Images show a large presence of military and plainclothes forces in various areas of Isfahan. Several citizens have been arrested. Streets are blocked and vehicles stopped.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for the Iranian Foreign Ministry, said Rafael Grossi has turned the International Atomic Energy Agency into a tool for political justification and war. He added that the agency's credibility as a neutral body has been damaged and it has played a role in political preparation for an illegal war. Baqaei also stated that responsibility for military attacks includes those who provide the political and legal basis for justification.

Turkey's Foreign Ministry welcomed the IAEA Board of Governors' decision to close Syria's nuclear file. Turkey stated that Damascus cooperated with the agency and showed transparency regarding activities during Bashar al-Assad's period. This news was reported by Farzia Sabti.

A citizen from Sabzevar reported that a power outage on September 10 caused his water heater to burn out. The repair costs amid economic difficulties have worsened his living conditions. He also mentioned the government's oppression and is awaiting a call from Reza Pahlavi.

Iran's security agencies have increased pressure and interrogations on the families of the missing national revolutionaries in various cities. Recently, several family members of protest victims have been summoned by phone or directly threatened. This report is based on information received by Iran International.

Ahmad Motahari-Asl, the Friday prayer leader of Tabriz, emphasized the enforcement of chastity and hijab laws. He called for decisive action against those promoting immorality. He also urged the government to support families and the values of chastity and hijab.

Fathollah Tavassoli, a member of parliament, demanded that Ahmad Donyamali, the Minister of Sports and Youth, explain his daughter's residence and activities in the UK. Tavassoli also announced that the number of signatures for the minister's impeachment has reached 43. He accused the minister of trying to prevent the impeachment process.

Nima Dadgostar from Iran International referred to a report showing that Iranian institutions use the 'Claude' model for propaganda, citizen surveillance, and identifying US military targets. Part of this usage is due to the regime's technical and economic incapacity. Some institutions use 'Claude' instead of an engineering team to develop malware and surveillance tools.

The Israeli Prime Minister displayed some of the weapons removed from southern Lebanon. These weapons include artillery, air defense, missiles, mines, and computer equipment. He stated that these weapons were supplied by the Islamic Republic and are now in Israeli hands.

On September 9, a citizen sent a video to Iran International criticizing the rising cost of medicine. Despite some items being covered by insurance, expenses continue to increase. Due to the heart disease of the family head, this person has taken on financial responsibilities and works from home.

Dozens of students at Birjand University who participated in the December 2025 protests have faced confrontation, summons, and expulsion. The protests began on December 3rd in South Khorasan and spread to six counties. Seba Heydarkhani has explained these protests and their suppression.

Esmail Baghaei, the spokesperson of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic, said at his Monday press conference that the talk about Mount Kolang Gazla is in line with America's media and psychological war and an uproar over nothing. He said the issue had also been raised about six or seven years ago during negotiations between the 13th government and the former US government. Baghaei added that Iran was not a member of the protocol then and is not now, and that under safeguards obligations it has informed the Agency of whatever has been or may be necessary.

Lotfollah Dejkam, the Friday prayer leader of Shiraz, stated that Iran's power has become global in some fields thanks to the sacrifices of martyrs and the efforts of the people. He emphasized that enemies have been defeated in the past and will be defeated again through the people's resistance. Dejkam said that continuing this path requires patience and perseverance.

Israel's Defense Minister Yisrael Katz announced that after destroying Hezbollah tunnels in southern Lebanon, the army is ready to target the group in new areas. He stated that the attack operations against Hezbollah will continue. These remarks were published by Iran International.

Months after the December protests, the spouses and fiancées of several missing persons shared images and stories of their grief and longing. These accounts show that the bullet that took their spouses' lives also changed their own lives forever. Farnoush Faraji, a member of Iran International's editorial team, reported on this.

Chris Wright, the US energy secretary, stated that oil tankers pass through the Strait of Hormuz under US naval escort. He said that leverage has been taken from the Islamic Republic. There is also no plan for uranium enrichment in Saudi Arabia.

Majid Parsa announced that 804 schools in Tehran are classified as worn-out spaces and need demolition and reconstruction. These schools have been structurally reinforced but do not meet the current needs of students. Tehran also faces deprivation in educational spaces and requires infrastructure development.

Ata Hosseinian stated that the government will remove subsidized gasoline quotas for newly registered cars priced over one billion tomans. Instead of a sudden price increase, the government will gradually reduce cheaper quotas. The goal is to replace cheaper quotas with 10,000 toman gasoline and reduce fuel subsidies.

Six commercial units in Khash County were sealed due to non-compliance with laws and regulations. Additionally, written warnings were issued to five other units. This action was carried out by the public places supervision officers.

A group of Iranians living in the UK gathered on Sunday, September 13, in front of the Prime Minister's building in London. They demanded the closure of the Islamic Republic's embassy. This news is based on videos received by Iran International.
